beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: In this town, there's a crack in the sky.
beats.visual: Wide night shot over foggy rooftops. Above the clock tower, a jagged glowing purple crack splits the sky, covered in giant strips of yellow tape.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: And every night at midnight, something tries to push it open.
beats.visual: The crack bulges outward and the tape strips strain. A curtain in a house window snaps shut.

beats.speaker: me
beats.text: HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS!
beats.visual: The clock tower hits midnight. Purple light flashes from the crack on every HUSS while giant grey fingertips poke through between the tape strips. Extras on the street dive indoors, shocked faces, and the camera shakes.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Five years ago, Mr. Hamble bumped the sky with a very tall ladder. Crack.
beats.visual: Day flashback: a ridiculously tall ladder leans on the clock tower, reaching into the clouds; Mr. Hamble (cap, grey mustache, overalls) at the top taps the sky and a purple crack zigzags out. He turns to camera, shocked face.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: So now, every night, one family gets Tape Duty.
beats.visual: The town square at dusk under a banner reading TAPE DUTY ROTA. The mayor hands a giant tape roll to a family like a trophy. They clap without much enthusiasm.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Climb the tower. Tape the crack. Never, ever look inside.
beats.overlay: RULE 1: CLIMB. RULE 2: TAPE. RULE 3: NEVER LOOK INSIDE.
beats.visual: A rules card appears line by line over a shot of the clock tower top with the crack overhead.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Mrs. Pell ran out of tape and used wrapping paper. The sky was festive for a week.
beats.visual: The crack is covered with red-and-green striped wrapping paper and a giant bow. Mrs. Pell (curly red hair, glasses) stands below, thumbs up, grin face.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: And Grandma's chewing gum is so sticky, the mayor has been stuck to a picnic table since spring.
beats.visual: Day cutaway in the park: the mayor (top hat, sash) sits on the picnic table bench, pink gum strings holding him in place. He waves sadly while leaves blow past. Grandma (white bun, glasses) chews proudly beside him.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: The pigeon flew in there once. He came back wearing sunglasses. He won't talk about it.
beats.visual: The pigeon sits alone on a park bench wearing tiny sunglasses, staring into the distance and not moving.

beats.speaker: me
beats.text: HUSS! HUSS! HUSS!
beats.visual: The camera zooms in three times, one step per HUSS, until the pigeon slowly turns its head to the lens.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Last night was our turn. But Dad pulled his back opening a jar.
beats.visual: Bedroom: Dad (brown beard, flannel shirt) lies flat on the floor in the crowdSurf pose, sweat face, an unopened pickle jar beside him. The kid (yellow raincoat, black hair) stands over him and crosses his arms.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: So it was me. Alone. Up the clock tower. At eleven fifty-eight.
beats.visual: Clock tower top at night: the kid stands at the edge in swirling fog, giant tape roll under one arm, the purple crack humming overhead. The clock face below reads 11:58.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: I pulled out the tape. Empty roll. Just cardboard.
beats.visual: Close-up: the kid lifts the roll and it is just a brown cardboard tube. He looks through it at the camera, shocked face.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Knock. Knock. Knock.
beats.visual: The crack pulses purple with each knock, and with each knock another tape strip peels off and flutters away into the fog.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: The crack split open. Giant fingers slid through. Long and grey, with way too many knuckles.
beats.visual: The crack splits wider. Four huge segmented grey fingers slide out and curl over its edge, every joint bending. Purple light pours down on the kid and the camera shakes hard.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: All I had in my pockets was homework, a sock, and Grandma's chewing gum.
beats.visual: Top-down shot of the kid's hands emptying his pockets: folded homework, a striped sock, a little pink pack of gum. The pack gets a glint.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: I chewed all twelve pieces at once. And I gummed that crack closed.
beats.visual: Back on the tower the kid chews with puffed cheeks, squint face, then leaps and slams a giant pink blob onto the crack, slam pose. The fingers flinch.

beats.speaker: me
beats.text: HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS!
beats.visual: With each HUSS the kid smears more pink gum along the crack, the grey fingers yank back inside, and the crack seals shut piece by piece. Town lights flick on and neighbours cheer from their windows.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Midnight. Silence. I did it.
beats.visual: Clock face reads 12:00. The kid stands in a cheer pose on the tower top, the crack now a quiet pink scar glowing softly. The fog clears.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Then I broke rule three. I looked inside.
beats.visual: The kid leans in close to one last tiny sliver in the crack, peer pose, one eye to the gap. Slow push in.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Phew. The ladder monsters almost got in again.

card.quote: Phew. The ladder monsters almost got in again.

beats.visual: Through the sliver: a dim purple space. A small grey blocky kid with too many knuckles presses tape over the crack from their side, sweat face, wiping its brow; behind it a GIANT grey grown-up hand (the fingers from before) lowers away, relieved. Only one huge grey eye of the grown-up is visible at the edge.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: The monsters. They meant us.
beats.visual: Slow pull back from the kid's frozen, shocked face, out past the tower and the tiny glowing town below, to the sealed crack in the black sky. Hold, then cut to black.
